From 11522448e641e8f1690c9db06e01985e8e19b401 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2020 15:14:30 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/603: Always fault when _PAGE_ACCESSED is not set

The kernel expects pte_young() to work regardless of CONFIG_SWAP.

Make sure a minor fault is taken to set _PAGE_ACCESSED when it
is not already set, regardless of the selection of CONFIG_SWAP.

Fixes: 84de6ab0e904 ("powerpc/603: don't handle PAGE_ACCESSED in TLB miss handlers.")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/a44367744de54e2315b2f1a8cbbd7f88488072e0.1602342806.git.christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/kernel/head_book3s_32.S b/arch/powerpc/kernel/head_book3s_32.S
index 5eb9eedac920..2aa16d5368e1 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/kernel/head_book3s_32.S
+++ b/arch/powerpc/kernel/head_book3s_32.S
@@ -457,11 +457,7 @@ InstructionTLBMiss:
 	cmplw	0,r1,r3
 #endif
 	mfspr	r2, SPRN_SPRG_PGDIR
-#ifdef CONFIG_SWAP
 	li	r1,_PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_ACCESSED | _PAGE_EXEC
-#else
-	li	r1,_PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_EXEC
-#endif
 #if defined(CONFIG_MODULES) || defined(CONFIG_DEBUG_PAGEALLOC)
 	bgt-	112f
 	lis	r2, (swapper_pg_dir - PAGE_OFFSET)@ha	/* if kernel address, use */
@@ -523,11 +519,7 @@ DataLoadTLBMiss:
 	lis	r1, TASK_SIZE@h		/* check if kernel address */
 	cmplw	0,r1,r3
 	mfspr	r2, SPRN_SPRG_PGDIR
-#ifdef CONFIG_SWAP
 	li	r1, _PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_ACCESSED
-#else
-	li	r1, _PAGE_PRESENT
-#endif
 	bgt-	112f
 	lis	r2, (swapper_pg_dir - PAGE_OFFSET)@ha	/* if kernel address, use */
 	addi	r2, r2, (swapper_pg_dir - PAGE_OFFSET)@l	/* kernel page table */
@@ -603,11 +595,7 @@ DataStoreTLBMiss:
 	lis	r1, TASK_SIZE@h		/* check if kernel address */
 	cmplw	0,r1,r3
 	mfspr	r2, SPRN_SPRG_PGDIR
-#ifdef CONFIG_SWAP
 	li	r1, _PAGE_RW | _PAGE_DIRTY | _PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_ACCESSED
-#else
-	li	r1, _PAGE_RW | _PAGE_DIRTY | _PAGE_PRESENT
-#endif
 	bgt-	112f
 	lis	r2, (swapper_pg_dir - PAGE_OFFSET)@ha	/* if kernel address, use */
 	addi	r2, r2, (swapper_pg_dir - PAGE_OFFSET)@l	/* kernel page table */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/powerpc/kernel/head_book3s_32.S`**
   - The code has been modified to always include the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag in the page table entry (PTE) initialization for TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) miss handlers, regardless of whether `CONFIG_SWAP` is defined or not.
   - Specifically, the conditional compilation blocks that check for `CONFIG_SWAP` have been removed. This means that the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag is now always set in the following sections:
     - In the `InstructionTLBMiss` handler, `_PAGE_ACCESSED` is now included in the PTE setup.
     - In the `DataLoadTLBMiss` handler, `_PAGE_ACCESSED` is also included.
     - In the `DataStoreTLBMiss` handler, `_PAGE_ACCESSED` is included as well.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes made in the `head_book3s_32.S` file are interconnected as they all aim to ensure that the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag is consistently set during TLB miss handling. This addresses the kernel's expectation for the `pte_young()` function to operate correctly regardless of the `CONFIG_SWAP` configuration.
- By removing the conditional checks for `CONFIG_SWAP`, the patch simplifies the logic and guarantees that the minor fault is always triggered to set the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag, thus fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the fix reference). This ensures that the behavior of the memory management system is reliable and consistent across different configurations.

Here is the commit message:
powerpc/603: Always fault when _PAGE_ACCESSED is not set

The kernel expects pte_young() to work regardless of CONFIG_SWAP.

Make sure a minor fault is taken to set _PAGE_ACCESSED when it
is not already set, regardless of the selection of CONFIG_SWAP.

Fixes: 84de6ab0e904 ("powerpc/603: don't handle PAGE_ACCESSED in TLB miss handlers.")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/a44367744de54e2315b2f1a8cbbd7f88488072e0.1602342806.git.christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the conditional handling of the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag in the TLB miss handlers, which depended on the `CONFIG_SWAP` configuration. When `CONFIG_SWAP` was not defined, the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag was not set, leading to incorrect behavior of the `pte_young()` function, which is expected to work regardless of the swap configuration. This inconsistency could result in the kernel not properly tracking page access, potentially leading to performance issues or incorrect memory management.

-#endif

```assembly

-#else
-	li	r1,_PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_EXEC
```

Reason:
The conditional handling of the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag based on the `CONFIG_SWAP` configuration means that when `CONFIG_SWAP` is not defined, the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag is omitted. This leads to the `pte_young()` function not being able to correctly determine if a page has been accessed, resulting in improper tracking of page access and potential performance issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```assembly
 	li	r1, _PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_ACCESSED
-#else
-	li	r1, _PAGE_PRESENT
-#endif
```
Reason:
By ensuring that the `_PAGE_ACCESSED` flag is always included in the page table entry setup, regardless of the `CONFIG_SWAP` configuration, the patch guarantees that the kernel can properly track page access. This change allows the `pte_young()` function to work correctly, ensuring consistent behavior and improved memory management.
